clue.text: Cava and fuel unfortunately take on English list price

indicators.note: When something turns out unfortunately it has not come out the way it was meant to, and neither do these letters.
To take something on is to accept it into what you already have, so the letter named joins the pool being mixed.

parts.note: anagram fodder, eight letters
e = English, the ninth letter joining in

explanation.surface: Sparkling wine and petrol have both gone up to what the English list says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunately' reads as a shopper's grumble about prices, which is the cover the setter wants for an instruction to jumble. Eight letters of shopping need a ninth from somewhere, and that is the E.
explanation.definitionFit: The face value of a ticket, a stamp or a share is the figure printed on it — the price it is listed at rather than what anyone pays.

clue.text: Large extra measure

parts.note: over means surplus, as in money left over at the end of the week
the size of a thing is the measure of how big it is

explanation.surface: A generous top-up poured on top of the usual measure.
explanation.walkthrough: Three words running as one phrase about a big drink, with nothing to mark where the definition stops. 'Extra' wants the sense of surplus, the over in 'left over'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oversize luggage or clothing is bigger than the standard allows, so the adjective stands in for 'large' unchanged.

clue.text: Gin cocktail bolstering writer after love split?

indicators.note: A cocktail is several things shaken together into something new, so the letters it governs are poured out in another order.
A bolster props something up from underneath, and in a down clue whatever props another piece sits below it.
After puts one piece later than another, so the thing it follows goes down first.

parts.note: love is the tennis score of nothing, written as the letter O
a pen is the writer in the sense of the implement
the three letters of GIN in a new order

explanation.surface: A cocktail props up an author whose love affair has ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love split' reads as a break-up, but its two words sit on opposite sides of the clue: love is the tennis nothing that starts the answer, split is the definition left standing alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening is a gap where something has parted — a split in the cloud, a split in a fence — the noun, not the act of opening.

clue.text: Magic word — say in the style of genius American claiming zenith

indicators.note: To claim a thing is to take it to yourself and keep hold of it, so the letters named close around what follows.

parts.note: a la is French for in the style of, as in a la carte
a genius in the classical sense is an attendant spirit, and the ka is the spirit of a person in ancient Egyptian belief
z is the astronomer's symbol for the zenith
am = American

explanation.surface: An invitation to talk like a brilliant American at the peak of his powers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Genius' is the Roman sense, a guardian spirit, which is what lets a two-letter Egyptian soul answer for it. 'Say' marks the definition as one magic word among several.
explanation.definitionFit: Alakazam is what a stage conjuror calls out as the trick lands, a stock magic word alongside abracadabra and hey presto.

clue.text: Suit designer passed

definitions.note: Spades is plural in form but names a single suit of the pack, so the singular definition is the natural way to point at it.

indicators.note: A designer takes the material to hand and works it into a shape it did not have, which is what happens to these letters.

parts.note: anagram fodder, six letters

explanation.surface: News that the man who designed the suit has died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit designer' looks like one job title and is not: 'Suit' stands alone as the definition, and the card sense is wanted rather than the tailored one. 'Passed' is the polite word for died.
explanation.definitionFit: Spades is one of the four suits in a pack of cards, the black one with the pointed leaf.

clue.text: British instrument brought up mineral, potentially

indicators.note: In a down clue what is brought up has been carried back towards the top, so its letters read upwards.

parts.note: b = British
the instrument is a lyre, the small harp of Greek antiquity, written upwards

explanation.surface: A British instrument hauled up out of the ground might be worth something.
explanation.walkthrough: A lyre turns up in crosswords far more often than in music, and here it arrives upside down. 'Potentially' marks the definition as the class, with the answer one named member of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Beryl is a mineral species in its own right, the stone that emerald and aquamarine are varieties of, so the general word points at one particular member.

clue.text: Burst of applause during rehearsal vocals

indicators.note: What happens during something happens inside it, so the letters sit unbroken within the words that follow.

parts.note: rehearSAL VOcals, running across the gap between the words

explanation.surface: The singers get a round of applause in the middle of a rehearsal.
explanation.walkthrough: Two long words side by side and a short answer is the shape to watch for. A salvo is properly a volley of guns fired together, and clapping borrows the word for the same suddenness.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo of applause is a volley of it, the whole room going off at once, the word carried over from artillery.

clue.text: Sleep app I abandoned to get fruity sort of desserts

indicators.note: Abandoned behaviour is wild and unrestrained, and letters let loose like that will not stay in the order they were given.

parts.note: anagram fodder, nine letters

explanation.surface: Someone has given up on the sleep-tracking app on their phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleep app' looks like a gadget and is only nine letters, and the I beside it is fodder rather than the solver. Three P's in that fodder are the giveaway.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple pies are the standard fruit pudding of a British menu, so the phrase names the class the answer sits in.

clue.text: Italian wine with a sour opening note

indicators.note: The opening of a word is the letter it starts with, the one you meet first.

parts.note: the word is taken at face value as the letter
the first letter of sour
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A faintly sour first impression from a glass of Italian wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Tasting language gives the setter his cover: 'sour', 'opening' and 'note' all belong in a wine note and none of them is used that way. Asti is the sparkling white made around the Piedmont town of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is the sweet sparkling wine of Asti in Piedmont, so the general phrase names it by where it comes from.

clue.text: Rector enthralled by warm-ups for organs?

indicators.note: To be enthralled is to be held captive by something, so this letter is kept inside the word that follows.

parts.note: heats are the qualifying rounds run before a final, and they open up to take the letter in
r = rector, the priest in charge of a parish

explanation.surface: A rector is captivated by the preliminary rounds of some competition.
explanation.walkthrough: The rector puts a church organ in the solver's head, and the question mark is there because the organs wanted are the ones that pump blood. Heats are the rounds before a final, not a warm-up exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart is the organ that drives the blood round the body, so the plural names a set of them.

clue.text: Use it to view in plain sight and nude — I say!

definitions.text: Use it to view in plain sight
definitions.note: The definition describes what the answer is for rather than giving a noun synonym; the answer is the 'it' the clue tells you to use.

parts.note: nude and naked are the same state of undress

indicators.note: Say asks for what the letter sounds like when spoken rather than how it is written.

parts.note: the pronoun I, said aloud, is the organ you see with

explanation.surface: A startled onlooker exclaims at someone standing about with no clothes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I say!' is the stock exclamation of British surprise, and the surprise is cover for a one-letter homophone. The definition is the whole first half of the clue, not a single noun.
explanation.definitionFit: What you can see with the naked eye is what you can see unaided, so the answer is exactly the thing you use to view something in plain sight.

clue.text: One who works wonders with CGI, animated in creative mania

indicators.note: Animation sets still pictures moving, and letters set moving like that come to rest somewhere new.
Creative work makes something that was not there before out of the material to hand, here the letters.

parts.note: anagram fodder, three letters
anagram fodder, five letters

explanation.surface: Computer-generated imagery dreamt up in a burst of wild creative energy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface flatters the special-effects crew and the answer is the older trade they get compared to. Both halves supply letters: CGI is fodder, not a film technique.
explanation.definitionFit: A magician works wonders in the strict sense, the wonder being the act itself, and the phrase is what we say of anyone who pulls off the impossible.

clue.text: Peel with relish

definitions.meaning: the coloured outer rind grated off a lemon or an orange for flavouring
the keen appetite you bring to something you enjoy doing

explanation.surface: Stripping the skin off a fruit with evident enjoyment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peel' is a noun here, not the verb the surface offers: the stuff grated off the lemon, not the act of removing it. Relish plays the same trick, a condiment on the plate and an appetite in the diner.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest is the grated citrus peel used for flavouring, and it is also the keen enjoyment you do a thing with, which is relish.

clue.text: Ramshackle let ruined break

indicators.note: A ramshackle building has its parts out of true and barely in place, which is how these letters are left.

parts.note: anagram fodder, nine letters

explanation.surface: A rented property has been wrecked by whoever was in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruined' is the word begging to be read as the instruction and it is fodder; the instruction is the adjective out in front. A let is a property rented out, which is what holds the surface together.
explanation.definitionFit: An interlude is the pause between two parts of a performance, so 'break' is the everyday word for the same gap.

clue.text: Whack on Japanese guitar — it plays tunes?

definitions.note: The definition describes what the machine does rather than naming it, and the question mark concedes that other things play tunes too.

indicators.note: Something laid on another thing follows it across the row, so the piece named first is written second.

parts.note: j = Japanese
a uke is a ukulele, the four-stringed little cousin of the guitar
to box someone is to whack them, as in boxing their ears

explanation.surface: A Japanese guitar gets a thump and starts producing music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whack' is the blow, and 'on' sends it to the end of the answer rather than the front. Hitting the machine to make it play is exactly what the surface pretends is happening to the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A jukebox is the coin-fed machine in a bar that plays whichever record is chosen, so the phrase says what it is for.

clue.text: Scraps of strange books keep Penelope essentially satisfied

indicators.note: To keep something is to hold on to it, so the letters named take it inside and shut it in.

parts.note: odd and strange both say out of the ordinary
Penelope is the setter of this puzzle, so she is me
NT is the New Testament, the second set of books in the Bible

indicators.note: The essence of a word sits at its very centre, so only the middle letter is wanted.

parts.note: the middle letter of the nine in satisfied

explanation.surface: Unusual books are all it takes to keep the setter happy.
explanation.walkthrough: Penelope is the name printed above the puzzle, so the setter is signing herself into her own grid. 'Essentially' takes a letter from the middle of a word rather than the gist of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddments are the leftover bits and pieces a shop or a workbox accumulates, which is what scraps are.

clue.text: Delightful morning chorus around Ullswater Head

indicators.note: What goes around a thing encloses it, so the letters named close over what follows.

parts.note: am is ante meridiem, the hours before midday

indicators.note: The head of a word is the letter standing at the front of it.

parts.note: the first letter of Ullswater, a lake in the English Lake District
to sing is what a chorus does

explanation.surface: Birdsong at dawn heard at the top end of a Lakeland water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Morning chorus' is one phrase on the surface and two separate pieces underneath, with the lake dropping in between them. Capitalising 'Head' makes it look like part of a place name.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amusing raises a smile, and delightful says the same of a story or an afternoon.

clue.text: Inadequate, backward, tardy places where males gather, perhaps

indicators.note: Something backward runs the other way, so the letters named are read from the last of them to the first.

parts.note: tardy and late both say behind time
a lek is the patch of ground where male birds such as black grouse gather to display for mates

explanation.surface: Backwaters where the men congregate get written off as poor and behind the times.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue opens as a string of adjectives, so 'backward' looks like another of them rather than the instruction. 'Perhaps' is there because the males doing the gathering are birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeletal service or a skeletal account is stripped to the bare bones, which is inadequate for what is being asked of it.

clue.text: High pitched sound overwhelming place for performing

indicators.note: To overwhelm a thing is to come down over it and cover it completely, so the letters named close over what follows.

parts.note: a ping is the thin high noise of a struck glass or a microwave finishing
to lay something down is to place it

explanation.surface: A shrill noise swamps the hall where the concert is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place for performing' looks like one phrase asking for a theatre and is two jobs: 'place' is the verb supplying the inner letters, 'performing' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A band playing is a band performing, and the two words swap in the same continuous tense.

clue.text: Pasty-faced director's staff

parts.note: a wan face is pale and drained of colour
d = director

explanation.surface: A pale film director's walking stick.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive sets the trap: 'staff' looks like the people a director employs and is the stick sense. The conjuror's staff is the one the puzzle's magic theme wants.
explanation.definitionFit: A wand is a slender rod, the staff carried by a conjuror or a fairy godmother.

clue.text: American spies circle around wood

indicators.note: To circle a thing is to go right round it, so the letters named open up and take it inside.

parts.note: a = American
ca is circa, Latin for around, used before an approximate date
the CIA is the American intelligence agency

explanation.surface: American agents ring a patch of woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circle around' reads as one action and carries two instructions: one says enclose, the other is the Latin tag for approximately. Acacia is the hard yellow-brown timber of the thorn tree, turned into bowls and furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Acacia is the close-grained timber of the thorn tree, sold as a hardwood, so the plain noun names what it is.

clue.text: Go study revolutionary to get inspired

indicators.note: A revolution turns a thing right round, so the letters named are read the other way about.

parts.note: to go is to leave
a den is the little room at home you study in, turned round

explanation.surface: Advice to go and read up on a revolutionary and come away fired up.
explanation.walkthrough: Bread is leavened when the yeast lifts it, and the figurative sense — a flat thing lightened and enlivened — is the one 'inspired' reaches for. 'Revolutionary' is a person on the surface and an instruction underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: To leaven is to lighten and enliven the way yeast raises dough, so a leavened speech is one inspired with some life.

clue.text: Great serves from Agassi, Clijsters, Evert and Sampras taking number one spots

indicators.note: Number one spot is the place at the very front, so each name gives up the letter standing there.

parts.note: the first letter of Agassi
the first letter of Clijsters
the first letter of Evert
the first letter of Sampras

explanation.surface: Four tennis champions who all reached the top of the world rankings.
explanation.walkthrough: Agassi, Clijsters, Evert and Sampras between them won tennis titles for three decades, and the clue wants nothing from any of them but an initial.
explanation.definitionFit: An ace is a serve the receiver never gets a racket to, the best thing a server can do with the ball.

clue.text: Search through Albuquerque streets

indicators.note: To go through something is to pass inside it, so the letters run on unbroken within the words that follow.

parts.note: AlbuquerQUE STreets, running across the gap between the words

explanation.surface: Hunting for something in the streets of Albuquerque.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Search through' reads as one phrasal verb, which hides the fact that the second word is the instruction. Albuquerque is the largest city in New Mexico, and its cluster of odd letters is the bait.
explanation.definitionFit: A quest is a search pursued with some determination, so the noun swaps straight in.

clue.text: Maybe Man City delivering, mercifully!

indicators.note: Maybe says the word beside it is only one possible instance, so what is wanted is the wider class it belongs to.

parts.note: a human is maybe a man, the wider class the example sits in
Ely is a city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Manchester City are finally producing the goods, thank goodness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man City' is the football club on the surface and two unrelated pieces underneath, with 'Maybe' governing the first word alone. Ely is tiny for a city, a cathedral in the Fens and little else, which is what makes it so useful to setters.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat someone humanely is to treat them with mercy and no cruelty, so the two adverbs cover the same ground.

clue.text: Plane originally landed yesterday, in an entirely bump-free way

parts.note: a plane surface is a flat and even one

indicators.note: Originally means at the outset, so each word gives up the letter it begins with.

parts.note: the first letter of landed
the first letter of yesterday

explanation.surface: An aircraft touched down yesterday without a single bump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' is the flat surface, not the aircraft the rest of the sentence promises, and the capital letter helps the disguise. One 'originally' reaches across two words for two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spread or done evenly goes on smoothly and without variation, which is a bump-free way of doing it.

clue.text: Deranged satanist's sidekick

indicators.note: To derange a thing is to disturb its arrangement, leaving its parts in no proper order.

parts.note: anagram fodder, nine letters counting the s after the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A devil-worshipper's unhinged helper.
explanation.walkthrough: An apostrophe is no barrier: the S after it counts as a letter of the fodder, which is how three words make nine. The magician's helper is what the puzzle's theme is after.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant works at someone's side in the supporting role, which is what a sidekick does.

clue.text: Rolls among others, dachshund on top, as tail wags

indicators.note: What sits on top of a word is the letter at the very front of it.

parts.note: a Rolls is one car among others, the make standing in for the class

indicators.note: The tail of a word is the letter on the end, the last one it trails.

parts.note: the first letter of dachshund
the last letter of as

explanation.surface: A dachshund perched on a Rolls in a line of parked cars, tail going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' is the smallest word in the clue and the one carrying a letter, which is what makes the ending hard to find. A card is a wag — 'he's a right card' — and the pack is where the puzzle's theme has been heading.
explanation.definitionFit: A card is an entertaining, larger-than-life character, so the plural answers to wags, the jokers of the party.
